6. Optimization Insights & Recommendations

Synthesizing findings into actionable recommendations for load balancing, queue management, pricing strategy adjustments, and renewable energy maximization.

REC-1: Demand-Shift Incentives for Peak → Off-Peak Hours

Peak-hour demand (84.1) exceeds off-peak (34.6) significantly. Introduce off-peak pricing discounts of 15–25% to shift discretionary charging sessions. Targeting a 10% shift could reduce peak station load by approximately 8.4 kW per station.

REC-2: Queue Relief at Highway Corridor Stations

Highway locations experience the highest wait times (9.6 min avg), particularly during Peak hours. Deploy 2–4 additional chargers per high-traffic Highway station and implement dynamic queue management with real-time availability notifications sent to approaching vehicles.

REC-3: Green Charging Windows

Renewable energy ratios peak during Clear conditions (35.7%) and Off-Peak hours (39.3%). Create "Green Charging" time windows with reduced rates during high-renewable periods to align EV charging with clean energy availability. This directly improves the renewable energy ratio KPI while reducing grid carbon intensity.

REC-4: Priority-Based Queue Management

The optimization reward is most favorable as priority increases — prioritize smart queue scheduling that minimizes wait times for high-priority vehicles while maintaining fair access. Use the optimization_reward metric as a real-time decision signal for charger assignment algorithms.

REC-5: Grid Load Balancing via Station-Level Dispatch

Station load varies significantly by day (53 kW on Friday vs 53 kW on Thursday). Implement station-level load caps during peak hours and route overflow demand to nearby underutilized stations. The scatter between charging power and station load confirms that managing charger power levels is an effective lever for grid stress reduction.
